title: TrustBound: A Mechanized Note on Payment-Epoch Completeness
abstract: Payment operations requested by an AI agent may remain executable, or their outcomes unresolved, after the agent has stopped. We study when a trusted payment service can account for every payment identity in an epoch and exclude further payments under earlier authority. Our Lean admission model records operations before granting execution authority and serializes both actions with an admission fence. We prove that fencing fixes a journal covering all modeled effects and outstanding rights. Discharging those rights prevents further effects; truthful outcomes for the recorded identities then establish exact accounting. A complementary provider-contract model requires registration before activation and keeps unregistered objects inert. We check its mapping to the admission model and test the proofs' dependence on key assumptions. Implementation evidence comprises six service histories checked in Lean, bounded operation schedules, and five scripted client behaviors. These experiments distinguish protection against repeated dispatch from the outcome evidence required for closure. The contribution is a payment-specific formalization of established closure principles with explicit trust assumptions and reproducible checks. Applying its guarantees to a deployed service requires evidence that the implementation and payment provider satisfy those assumptions.
